research_question: In hospitalised adult patients, does medication review (pharmacist-led or multidisciplinary systematic review of a patient's medicines) compared with standard care reduce all-cause mortality at the longest available follow-up?
treatment_label: Medication review (systematic pharmacist-led or multidisciplinary review of the patient's medications, with or without recommendations/follow-up) delivered during hospitalisation
control_label: Standard/usual hospital care without a structured medication review
outcome_description: All-cause mortality (death from any cause) among hospitalised adult patients, taken at the longest available follow-up reported in each study. Number of deaths / total participants per arm, or a reported effect estimate for death from any cause.
positive_direction: A positive Hedges g (favourable effect) means patients receiving medication review had LOWER all-cause mortality than patients receiving standard care.
search_queries: medication review hospitalised patients randomised controlled trial mortality
pharmacist-led medication review inpatients usual care trial outcomes
clinical medication review deprescribing hospital admission mortality effect
inclusion_criteria: Study enrolled adult patients (mostly 18+) who were hospitalised or admitted to hospital (including at admission or discharge)
Study evaluated some form of medication review / medication optimisation intervention compared with standard or usual care
Study reports quantitative data on all-cause mortality (deaths per arm, or an effect estimate such as RR/OR/HR with variance) at any follow-up
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, editorial, commentary, opinion, protocol, or purely theoretical/modelling paper)

No comparison between a medication review intervention group and a standard-care control group (e.g. single-arm, before-after with no control, or head-to-head comparison of two different medication review models only)
No quantitative outcome data from which an effect size can be computed (no counts/proportions, means+SDs, t/F statistics, or odds/risk/hazard ratios)
Completely unrelated to medication review in hospitalised adults, or reports no all-cause mortality data (e.g. only readmissions, ED contacts, adverse drug events, or quality of life)
moderators_to_extract: Intervention provider (clinical pharmacist alone vs multidisciplinary team vs physician-led)
Intervention intensity (single in-hospital review vs review plus post-discharge follow-up)
Patient population (general medical, geriatric/frail, cardiology, polypharmacy-selected)
Sample size category and country/health-system setting
effect_size_note: Mortality is a binary outcome; extract deaths/total per arm (or a reported RR/OR/HR with CI) at the longest available follow-up per study, and convert to the common effect metric with the standard log-odds-to-Hedges-g transformation where needed. Sign is oriented so that fewer deaths in the medication review arm yields a positive effect.
